compute.anchor_note: Compute density per mm2 is derived from one published GPU's dense tensor roofs divided by its published whole-die area, then scaled by the node logic-density ratio. Applying a whole-die-derived density to a modelled design's COMPUTE-ONLY area is the model's stated compute assumption: it is conservative in that an A100 die spends area on HBM PHY, L2 and schedulers that the density is nevertheless charged for, and optimistic in that NVIDIA's tensor cores are a highly tuned datapath. Newer parts are denser: B200 achieves 2.81e12 FP8 ops/s/mm2 at 4NP against 1.50e12 predicted by scaling A100 INT8, so this anchor understates a 2026 design by roughly 1.9x.

bf16.note: A100 80GB SXM, 312 TFLOPS dense BF16 tensor (624 with structured sparsity, not used)

fp4.note: A100 publishes 1248 TOPS dense INT4; FP4 e2m1 is taken as the same datapath area as INT4

fp8.note: A100 publishes 624 TOPS dense INT8. An FP8 e4m3 multiply-accumulate is taken as the same datapath area as INT8; A100 itself has no FP8 unit, so this is a density transfer, not a claim about Ampere.

w4a8_density_rule.note: A 4-bit-weight by 8-bit-activation multiply-accumulate is bounded below by the w8a8 datapath (no narrowing credit taken) and above by the w4a4 datapath. NVIDIA publishes both endpoints on one die, so the bracket is published and only the interpolation is a judgement. Both endpoints are also reported so the bracket, not the midpoint, is what the reader checks.

compute.note: fraction of the peak tensor roof a real decode kernel sustains, covering pipeline bubbles, tail effects and non-tensor interleave
compute.source: carried over from src/opentallas/schema.py ArchitectureProfile default

expert_router_imbalance.note: Multiplier on the per-region sweep depth, applied ON TOP OF the expected busiest-region load rather than instead of it. This replaces efficiencies.expert_load_balance = 0.85, which was documented as carrying 'the sweep depth is set by the busiest region rather than the mean' while the code divided the MEAN engaged-region load by it. The busiest region is now computed explicitly (roofline.expected_max_region_load), and a single constant cannot stand in for it: the ratio of the busiest region to the mean runs from 1.0 at batch 1 to about 3.0 at batch 64. What is left for this parameter is the residual imbalance of a TRAINED router against the uniform-random draw the busiest-region statistic assumes. It is 1.0 -- the neutral value, which makes it inert -- because no trace exists to set it, and because a parameter must not take its value from the answer it is wanted to produce. The per-region sweep depth is exactly linear in it, so a trace showing a 1.3x hot-expert bias moves every per-region number by 1.3x.
expert_router_imbalance.source: no measured routing trace for a per-region compute-in-ROM fabric

hbm_bandwidth.note: 0.90 of peak HBM bandwidth sustained, applied to both weight and KV traffic on ANY device with HBM -- the GPU comparators and the ROM designs whose KV store is HBM alike, which is why this is not a one-sided credit. WAS 0.85 with no cited measurement at all. The two readings behind 0.90 are an A100 PCIe 40GB measured at 90.5% of its 1555 GB/s and an H800 memory controller measured at 91.3% on the same 2039 GB/s HBM2e configuration as the modelled A100 SXM part. NOT IMPLEMENTED, DELIBERATELY: the proposed read-only versus mixed split. Luo's method is already a mixed 5-read-to-1-write coalesced stream, so splitting it would double-count the write penalty. AND THE A100 WEIGHT-BOUND VALIDATION GATE IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THIS NUMBER: that gate is constructed to reproduce a published rate and would move with any efficiency, so quoting it here would be circular. DIRECTION: favours the GPU, about 0.982x on the headline.
hbm_bandwidth.source: Luo et al., Benchmarking and Dissecting the Nvidia Hopper GPU Architecture, IPDPS 2024, arXiv:2402.13499 (H800 memory controller 91.3% of 2039 GB/s HBM2e) ; NVIDIA A100 PCIe 40GB STREAM-class measurements at 90.5% of 1555 GB/s. No vendor states a sustained fraction for either part.

hbm_capacity.note: fraction of physical HBM available to checkpoint and KV after runtime workspace, allocator and safety reserve
hbm_capacity.source: carried over from src/opentallas/schema.py ArchitectureProfile default

no_clock_derate_rationale.note: No separate clock-efficiency derate is applied anywhere in this model. A100's 312 TFLOPS, WSE-2's 20 PB/s and the HBM bandwidths are achieved rates at shipping clocks, not timing-signoff targets, so charging a further clock derate on top would double-count. The only derates applied are the sustained-fraction ones named above.
no_clock_derate_rationale.source: definition of what this model's densities are derived from, WITH THE PREVIOUS CLAIM WITHDRAWN. The previous source field read "every density in this table is derived from an ACHIEVED shipping-silicon figure". That is FALSE for the ROM lane -- `rom.read_bandwidth_anchor` is YOLoC, which is SPICE-simulated with another paper's periphery grafted on and was never fabricated -- and UNVERIFIABLE for the SRAM lane, whose Cerebras 20 PB/s citation is dead (cerebras.ai/chip today describes WSE-3 only, at 21 PB/s; the string "20 PB" does not appear). The A100 and HBM figures ARE achieved shipping-silicon rates and the rationale holds for them.

rom_read_bandwidth.note: Fraction of the ROM array's peak sweep rate sustained in practice. A mask-ROM sweep is the most regular access pattern available -- a compile-time-fixed linear walk of the whole array with no arbitration, no conflicts and no refresh -- so 0.75 is a conservative charge and 0.90-1.00 is arguable. The study reports the underated ceiling alongside it because this derate moves the ROM answer directly.

sram_read_bandwidth.note: fraction of the SRAM array's peak read rate sustained by a real gather pattern

stage_balance.note: penalty applied to a multi-device pipeline for imperfect layer balance across devices
stage_balance.source: no measured layer-to-device partition for the modelled designs

hbm_j_per_byte.note: 13.11 pJ/bit = 104.88 pJ/byte at the HBM level on a shipping A100 40GB (N7, Perlmutter), measured by microbenchmark regression and published at SC'25. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, 3.36x UP from the 31.2 pJ/B this entry used to carry. The incumbent was O'Connor's HBM2-era DRAM-DEVICE-ONLY model figure; this one is measured and its boundary is the whole HBM path -- DRAM device, TSV, interposer, processor-side PHY and the memory controller (the paper's Fig. 1 caption states verbatim that 'memory controller energy is tabulated with HBM energy'). Scope is beyond-L2 only: the paper subtracts separately-extracted L1 and L2 parameters (its Eq. 8), so per-byte SM front-end and address-generation overheads cancel out of this number rather than hiding inside it. 65% of the A100 figure (8.47 of 13.11 pJ/bit) is CONTROL PLANE -- controllers, addresses, row decoders, tag lookups -- so charging a non-GPU memory subsystem a GPU's control plane is an extrapolation and the range must be swept, not asserted. The range is the spread across the paper's four measured parts (GH200 11.68, A100 13.11, MI250X GCD 13.64, MI300A 14.72 pJ/bit); it is NOT an uncertainty band for a non-GPU part. Two further costs this term does NOT carry and the model still does not charge: L1/L2 traversal (a further 6.30 pJ/bit on the A100 for streaming traffic, same paper) and the device's traffic-independent power (the same paper's Table 2 publishes P_const = 54 W for the A100, which is what power.clocked_idle_floor_w_per_device now carries).
hbm_j_per_byte.source: https://escholarship.org/content/qt6189368s/qt6189368s.pdf -- Measuring the Energy of Data Movement on Modern GPU Systems, SC 2025, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, Table 3

bf16.note: 0.33 pJ per operation for a 16-bit multiply-accumulate datapath. WAS 1e-13, which is 3.3x below the MEASURED datapath plane of a shipping N7 tensor core and 2.1x below Horowitz's 45 nm FP16 MAC -- a 7 nm number below a 45 nm one. Antepara et al., SC'25 Table 3 measures the A100 Matrix-FP16 path at control 0.37 / datapath 0.33 / total 0.70 pJ/FLOP. GRADED `assumed`, NOT `derived`, AND THE REASON IS THE WHOLE POINT: taking the datapath plane and dropping the control plane has no published basis -- a real MAC array pays some of its own instruction issue, operand collection and scheduling -- so this value stands on a BRACKET (1.3e-13 datapath-only at a better node, 7.0e-13 total) and not on a derivation. Sweep 1.3e-13 to 7.0e-13. DIRECTION: raises arithmetic energy on BOTH sides; Qwen3-8B is 100% bf16 in these studies and no other model uses it.
bf16.source: Antepara, Williams et al., Measuring the Energy of Data Movement on Modern GPU Systems, SC'25, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, Table 3 (A100 Matrix-FP16: control 0.37 / datapath 0.33 / total 0.70 pJ/FLOP) ; Horowitz, Computing's Energy Problem, ISSCC 2014, for the 45 nm cross-check

fp32.note: 1.09 pJ per operation for a 32-bit floating-point datapath. WAS 4e-13. Same SC'25 table times Horowitz's 45 nm FP32-to-FP16 MAC ratio, and the arithmetic is stated so it can be checked: HOROWITZ'S 45 nm 32-bit float MULT IS 3.7 pJ, NOT 4 -- verified through EIE (arXiv:1602.01528) Table I, on which Horowitz is a co-author -- so the FP32 MAC is 4.6 pJ and the FP32/FP16 ratio is 3.29, giving 3.3e-13 x 3.29 = 1.09e-12. The 1.2e-12 first proposed is 6-14% high on its own formula. Sweep 4e-13 (the incumbent, kept as the floor) to 1.07e-11 (the A100 Vector-FP32 TOTAL in the same table); the gap between 1.09e-12 and 1.07e-11 is the honest measure of how much of a GPU FP32 FLOP is not arithmetic. Carries 0.06% of DeepSeek-V4-Pro's operations and nothing else in either study.
fp32.source: Antepara, Williams et al., SC'25, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, Table 3 ; Horowitz, Computing's Energy Problem, ISSCC 2014, as reproduced in Han et al., EIE, arXiv:1602.01528, Table I (45 nm 32-bit float MULT 3.7 pJ, ADD 0.9 pJ)

fp4.note: 0.023 pJ per operation for a 4-bit multiply-accumulate datapath. WAS 1.5e-14. Evidentially the cleanest leg in the ladder: Keller et al. Table 2 measures INT4 at 91.1 TOPS/W against INT8 at 39.1 TOPS/W on ONE FABRICATED DIE, both at 0.46 V, both at 50% density, on two dedicated datapaths -- so process, PVT, leakage and dataflow all cancel and the energy ratio is 0.4292. More conservative than argued: the pure-datapath ratio is nearer 0.38. LIKE fp8, IT MOVES NOTHING -- zero operations at every point in either study. Sweep 1.5e-14 (the incumbent) to 2.9e-14.
fp4.source: Keller et al., 2022 Symposium on VLSI Technology and Circuits, Digest pp. 16-17, Table 2 (fabricated TSMC 5nm: INT4 91.1 and INT8 39.1 TOPS/W at 0.46 V), https://d1qx31qr3h6wln.cloudfront.net/publications/C02-1.PDF

fp8.note: 0.054 pJ per operation for an 8-bit multiply-accumulate datapath. WAS 3e-14. Same SC'25 bf16 plane times Horowitz's INT8/FP16 ratio, cross-checked against Keller et al. (2022 Symp. VLSI Tech. & Circuits, Table 2), a FABRICATED TSMC 5nm die measuring INT8 at 39.1 TOPS/W at 0.46 V. Best-sourced rung in the ladder AND IT MOVES NOTHING IN EITHER STUDY: `points[].operations_by_canonical_format` charges fp8 on ZERO operations at every point. Sweep 3e-14 (the incumbent) to 6.8e-14.
fp8.source: Antepara, Williams et al., SC'25, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, Table 3 ; Keller et al., A 95.6-TOPS/W Deep Learning Inference Accelerator with Per-Vector Scaled 4-bit Quantization in 5nm, 2022 Symposium on VLSI Technology and Circuits, Digest pp. 16-17, Table 2, https://d1qx31qr3h6wln.cloudfront.net/publications/C02-1.PDF

w4a8.note: 0.039 pJ per operation for a 4-bit-weight by 8-bit-activation datapath, AND IT IS AN INTERVAL RATHER THAN A VALUE. THIS RUNG CARRIES 99.9% OF THIS STUDY'S OPERATIONS AND HAS NO SOURCE OF ANY KIND: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 is 99.94% w4a8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash is 99.86% w4a8, and no published or measured mixed 4-bit-weight by 8-bit-activation MAC energy exists at any node. The interval [2.33e-14, 5.42e-14] is bounded below by the fp4 rung and above by the fp8 rung, which share the accumulator; the point 3.9e-14 is their arithmetic mean and is a MIDPOINT, not an estimate. Read the interval and not the point. The evidence in this whole domain was spent almost exactly inversely to where it matters -- fp8 and fp4, the two rungs with fabricated silicon behind them, are charged on zero operations.
w4a8.source: no source of any kind exists for a mixed 4-bit-weight x 8-bit-activation MAC energy; the interval is bounded by this file's own fp4 and fp8 rungs, which share the accumulator

operand_delivery_j_per_byte.note: 0.23 pJ/byte to get one byte from the array that holds it to the arithmetic that consumes it, at a 7 nm-class node. This is the term docs/TECHNICAL_DIRECTION_RECOMMENDATION.md 0.11 named as missing: a Horowitz-class MAC energy is the ALU, not the cost of delivering its operands, and rom_read_j_per_byte's stated boundary stops at the macro output latch. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, 1.5x DOWN from the submitted 3.43e-13 -- the submitted wire constant used alpha x C x V^2 with alpha = 0.5 transitions/bit, which double-counts the transition: supply energy for one full 0->1->0 cycle is C*V^2, so energy per transition is (1/2)C*V^2 and the correct coefficient for random data is 0.25, not 0.5. The corrected form is anchored, not chosen: 0.25 x 0.2 pF/mm x (0.75 V)^2 x 1.6 repeater overhead = 0.045 pJ/bit/mm, and the same formula run at 45 nm/1.0 V returns 0.080 pJ/bit/mm against Dally's published 45 nm figure of 6 pJ to move 64 bits 1 mm = 0.094 pJ/bit/mm, an 18% agreement the submitted form missed by 1.7x. Point = one register-file/operand-collector access at N7 (0.091 pJ/B, Horowitz 45 nm scaled by 5.49x) + 0.40 pJ/B/mm over a 0.35 mm tile pitch. BOUNDARY, and the writer must not lose it: this scalar is the TILE-LOCAL FLOOR. The long-path ladder -- HBM to L2 to register file on an A100 is 8.3-10.0 pJ/B over 10-14.4 mm -- is NOT represented. Applied uniformly to weight and KV bytes it charges the ROM side ~1.6x on its dominant term and the GPU side ~1.01x on its dominant term, so the single number penalises the ROM side; that is the safe direction and it is why a scalar is shippable. THE 5.49x 45nm->N7 NODE FACTOR IS NOW UNSOURCED AND THE VALUE IS UNCHANGED ONLY BECAUSE NOTHING BETTER EXISTS. It was derived as "the geometric mean of ratios implied by this file's own mac_energy_j_per_op entries"; that ladder has since been re-anchored on a measured SC'25 A100 table and the ratios it implies are different, so the sentence that produced 5.49 is FALSE as written and must not be repeated. The honest interval for that factor is 2.1x-5.5x, which puts this entry at 2.3e-13 (kept, the low end) to 3.8e-13. It is left at the low end rather than raised because the term is applied uniformly to weight and KV bytes and therefore charges the ROM side about 1.6x on its dominant term against about 1.01x on the GPU's -- raising it would be a further charge against the ROM side that no source supports, and lowering the reported band is not on offer either. SRAM energy scales worse than logic, so if anything this understates the storage-level terms.
operand_delivery_j_per_byte.source: Horowitz, Computing's Energy Problem, ISSCC 2014 (register-file and cache access energies at 45 nm) ; Dally, published 45 nm wire energy, 64 bits x 1 mm = 6 pJ ; repeatered global wire C ~= 0.2 pF/mm at a leading node. NOT sourced to Sze et al. arXiv:1703.09039: that paper's Fig. 22 is NORMALISED ONLY (ALU 1x, RF 1x, NoC 2x, buffer 6x, DRAM 200x) and contains no pJ figure, so it cannot support any absolute constant and the earlier citation of it was a misreading.

rom_read_j_per_byte.note: 0.08 pJ/byte at N6 for the ROM read primitive -- address decode, wordline, bitline develop, sense/sample and macro output latch -- excluding the arithmetic, which roofline.py charges separately as mac_energy_j_per_op. VERIFIER-CORRECTED grade, not value: submitted as `derived` at 8e-14 and REGRADED to `assumed`, because the derivation behind it did not survive. It rests on the geometric centre of two methods that disagree by ~5x over a 17x-wide bracket (~0.02 to ~0.35 pJ/B), which is a point estimate, not a derivation. What the bracket is built from: (a) six published ROM/compute-in-ROM macros' TOPS/W scaled by node and V^2 -- but at most THREE of the six are fabricated silicon (BitROM is post-layout, YOLoC is SPICE with peripherals estimated from a different paper and publishes NO supply voltage at all, DCiROM claims no measurement), and a CiM macro's TOPS/W includes the arithmetic this boundary excludes, so that method measures something strictly LARGER than the term; (b) a 130 nm mask-ROM tile read of 1.20 pJ per sensed ternary weight = 4.80 pJ/B, scaled by (0.75/1.80)^2 and by a cell-to-cell area ratio of 14.3, giving ~0.02-0.09 pJ/B at N6. THE DIRECTION MATTERS: this is 6.25x BELOW the 0.5 pJ/byte this entry used to carry, so adopting it makes the Taalas HC1 power gate WORSE, not better. It is adopted anyway because the evidence points there. The 0.5 pJ/B it replaces was a schema default with no evidence at all.
rom_read_j_per_byte.source: Yin et al., JSSC 2023 and JSSC 2025 (doi:10.1109/JSSC.2025.3556008); Cheong et al., A-SSCC 2024; YOLoC, GLSVLSI 2022 (doi:10.1145/3489517.3530576, simulated, supply voltage unpublished); BitROM, ASP-DAC 2026 (post-layout); Ankhdjet 130 nm mask-ROM tile read, arXiv:2608.26206 Table VII (1.20 pJ per ternary weight at tt/27C/1.80V). No fabricated leading-node mask-ROM macro reports read energy at the macro boundary separately from compute.

sram_read_j_per_byte.note: 2.6 pJ per byte read from an on-die SRAM array, EXPLICITLY A FLOOR. WAS 1e-12 with "no vendor macro energy published". SC'25 Table 3 measures the A100 L1 at control 1.26 / datapath 0.33 / total 1.59 pJ/bit, which is 2.64 / 12.72 pJ/B. This entry takes 2.6e-12 -- the datapath plane plus the part of the control plane an SRAM unavoidably pays -- and LABELS IT A FLOOR, because the dropped control plane contains row decode, which a scratchpad does pay. GRADED `assumed`, NOT `derived`: the plane split has no published basis, exactly as for the MAC ladder. WHERE IT IS CHARGED AND WHY THAT MATTERS FOR FAIRNESS: only when `kv_store == 'sram'`, which is the ROM-side designs; the A100's and B200's KV is HBM at 104.88 pJ/B and is untouched by this entry. So raising it charges the ROM side and not the GPU side -- it FAVOURS THE GPU, which is why it is applied at the measured floor rather than at the datapath plane. Sweep 1.44e-12 (the MI250X L1 datapath plane in the same table, the most favourable reading anywhere) to 1.27e-11 (the A100 L1 total).
sram_read_j_per_byte.source: Antepara, Williams et al., Measuring the Energy of Data Movement on Modern GPU Systems, SC'25, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, Table 3 (A100 L1: control 1.26 / datapath 0.33 / total 1.59 pJ/bit; MI250X L1 datapath 0.18 pJ/bit)

interconnect_area_fraction.note: on-die network and the bank-to-compute fabric that multiplexes ROM banks onto the shared compute array. Sweep 0.05 to 0.15.
interconnect_area_fraction.source: no published floorplan for a mask-ROM inference die

overhead_area_fraction.note: host/PCIe PHY, clocking and PLLs, power delivery structures, control, DFT and scan. Sweep 0.06 to 0.15.
overhead_area_fraction.source: no published floorplan for a mask-ROM inference die

grade_definitions.assumed: no published value found; a stated judgement that must be swept
grade_definitions.derived: computed from published/measured entries by a formula stated in the note
grade_definitions.executed: obtained by running something in this repository -- the reference oracle, a deployment, a campaign -- with the artifact holding the numbers committed and named in the entry's `artifact` field. Distinct from `measured`, which means fabricated silicon in a peer-reviewed venue; almost nothing this program does is that, and its absence was pushing executed values into grades that fitted them worse.
grade_definitions.measured: taken from fabricated silicon reported in a peer-reviewed venue
grade_definitions.published: stated by the vendor or standards body for a shipping part or process

max_beachfront_utilization.note: A100 80GB places five HBM2e stacks on an 826 mm2 die: 5 x 12 mm of pitch against a 115 mm perimeter, or 52%. Shipping parts therefore use roughly 50-60% of the die edge for HBM, the rest going to host, scale-up and power. 0.60 is taken as the ceiling, which makes a modelled ROM part's HBM beachfront no more aggressive than NVIDIA's own. This matters: at equal die area both sides then have the SAME KV bandwidth ceiling, and the ROM part's advantage is only that it does not also spend that bandwidth on weights.

phy_area_mm2_per_stack.note: A 1024-bit HBM PHY plus controller is commonly quoted between 8 and 15 mm2 at 7 nm class. Sweep that range.
phy_area_mm2_per_stack.source: no vendor-published HBM PHY macro area

stack_beachfront_mm.note: 11 mm HBM package edge plus routing keep-out; carried over from configs/hardware/technology_inputs.json

stack_capacity_bytes.note: A100 80GB carries five active HBM2e stacks; 80 GB / 5

Shipping parts therefore use roughly 50-60% of the die edge for HBM, the rest going to host, scale-up and power. 0.60 is taken as the ceiling, which makes a modelled ROM part's HBM beachfront no more aggressive than NVIDIA's own. This matters: at equal die area both sides then have the SAME KV bandwidth ceiling, and the ROM part's advantage is only that it does not also spend that bandwidth on weights.

phy_area_mm2_per_stack.source: no vendor-published HBM PHY macro area

published_stack_ceiling.note: Micron HBM3E: over 1.2 TB/s per stack, 24 GB at 8-high and 36 GB at 12-high. Retained as the upper cross-check on the shipping-system-derived values above; not used by the model.

stack_bandwidth_bytes_s.note: B200 SXM delivers 8 TB/s across eight HBM3E stacks: 8 TB/s / 8. Micron publishes over 1.2 TB/s per HBM3E stack at full pin speed (https://www.micron.com/products/memory/hbm/hbm3e), so 1.0 TB/s is the rate a shipping system actually clocks and is the conservative choice.

stack_beachfront_mm.note: 11 mm x 11 mm HBM3E package plus routing keep-out

stack_capacity_bytes.note: B200 SXM ships 180 GB across eight HBM3E stacks: 180 GB / 8. Micron's published HBM3E 12-high part is 36 GB per stack (https://www.micron.com/about/blog/applications/ai/micron-continues-memory-industry-leadership-with-hbm3e-12-high-36gb), so this is the SHIPPING-SYSTEM figure rather than the densest available die stack. Deriving it from the reference GPU keeps both sides of the iso-area comparison on identical memory technology, which is the point.

hbm.note: 32 bytes, the sector NVIDIA states its memory system moves. WAS `assumed` and reconstructed from HBM3 pseudo-channel geometry ("a 32-bit pseudo-channel at burst 8"), which happened to give the same number by a route the vendor does not state. NVIDIA states the 32-byte sector directly, so this is `published`. DELETED: the previous note's "A 68-byte index entry therefore costs 96 bytes" -- that example used an index entry size this model does not carry and is retracted along with the 1.6x sensitivity in `kv.index_layout`.
hbm.source: https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/ProfilingGuide/index.html#memory-chart -- NVIDIA Nsight Compute Kernel Profiling Guide, memory chart / metrics section, which defines the sector as a 32-byte aligned region of device memory and reports device-memory traffic in those units; cross-checked against https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/ on coalescing granularity

sram.note: The row width a wide on-die SRAM macro delivers per access. 128 bytes is a common leading-node macro word for a bandwidth-optimised array; a narrower 64-byte macro halves the waste on a 68-byte entry only because 68 still spills into a second word. Sweep 64 to 256.
sram.source: no vendor macro datasheet for the target on-die arrays

index_layout.note: Where a compressed-sparse layer's index entry sits relative to the payload entry it describes. 'interleaved' is the natural result of writing both at generation time and makes every index entry its own access; 'contiguous' packs the index array separately so the scan is one sequential run and granule rounding costs nothing. RETRACTED: the previous note's "The two differ by more than 1.6x on DeepSeek-V4-Flash at 200K context". At the entry sizes this model actually carries the two layouts coincide, and the 1.6x was computed against a 68-byte index entry that is not what the profile declares. Stated as a named choice because a design can simply choose the cheap one -- and because a model that silently assumed the cheap one would be claiming a design decision as a fact.
index_layout.source: layout CHOICE, not a physical constant; no released serving implementation inspected for this program

kv.purpose: How KV bytes are actually moved, as opposed to how many the algorithm needs. workload.kv_traffic counts algorithmic bytes; a memory system moves whole granules, and for a sparse-index model most of the KV read is a scan of entries far smaller than one granule.

array_pass_boundaries_per_layer.note: Serially dependent matrix passes in one decoder layer, and THE DEFAULT ONLY. This entry is now per model: `latency.array_pass_boundaries_per_layer_by_model` names the value for each model the studies run, and `tools/run_roofline_studies.py` applies it and REFUSES a model that is not named there. A single constant cannot be right for two architectures whose layers have different serial chains, and the previous flat 4.0 undercharged DeepSeek by exactly one pass. This default remains the standard dense block -- QKV, attention output, gate/up, down -- and is what an unlisted model would get if the refusal above did not exist. Graded `assumed` rather than `derived` because the model profiles do not state a pass structure: `operations.operation_inventory` counts arithmetic, not passes. STATE WHICH QUANTITY THIS IS: serial dependency depth, not array occupancy. The same layer honestly yields 4, 5 or 8 depending on which you name -- independent descriptors pipeline rather than each paying a drain -- and 8-9 is the occupancy reading, which is why `range_high` stops at 5.
array_pass_boundaries_per_layer.source: transformer block structure: QKV, attention output, gate/up, down

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731.note: 5. DeepSeek-V4's decoder layer adds a serially dependent router pass -- the expert scores must exist before the expert matrices can be selected and started -- on top of the four of the standard block. Derived from the graph contract the compiler emits for this model rather than from the profile, which counts arithmetic and not passes; graded `assumed` because a graph reading is a hypothesis about serial depth and not a measurement of one. NOT GRADED `derived`: no committed artifact in this repository counts serially dependent matrix passes for any model, so there is nothing to derive from by a stated formula.
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731.source: DeepSeek-V4 decoder graph as compiled by compiler/backends/rom: QKV, attention output, router score, expert gate/up, expert down

DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813.note: 5, by the declared Flash->Pro architectural analogy that the rest of this program already runs on: Pro is the same decoder layer at a larger width and expert count, so its serial chain is Flash's. If that analogy is ever broken this entry must be re-derived rather than inherited.

latency.purpose: The serial per-layer cost that no amount of bandwidth removes. EVERY TERM HERE IS DERIVED FROM A PRIMITIVE THAT EXISTS INDEPENDENTLY OF THE TAALAS HC1 ANCHOR, and each carries range_low/range_high. The anchor gate is evaluated at both ends of that band and reports where it lands as an OUTCOME. VERIFIER-CORRECTED ON THE VALUE AND ON TWO VERBATIM DOCUMENTARY ERRORS, both of which were duplicated word for word into `links.infiniband_ndr`. (1) The previous note read "De Sensi et al. (SC24) measured 3.7-5.7 us across FIVE production supercomputers"; the abstract reads "This paper comprehensively characterizes THREE supercomputers -- Alps, Leonardo, and LUMI" and Table I has three columns. (2) The previous note read "on LEONARDO (A100 + HDR InfiniBand) 4.33 us within one switch rising to 5.56 us across switches"; SS V-B.1 reads "(from 4.33us to 5.56us ON ALPS), whereas ON LEONARDO it increases by 2x (from 2.03us to 4.23us)". Alps is H100 + HPE Slingshot-11, an ETHERNET Dragonfly. So the entry that prices this study's scale-out fabric was carrying an Ethernet machine's number under an InfiniBand machine's name, and it was 2.13x too slow. STATED AT 2.03 us: Leonardo same-switch, which is the A100 + HDR InfiniBand machine this study actually models, measured on fabricated silicon in a peer-reviewed venue. The band is set by this file's own convention for `nvlink3`/`nvlink5` -- best measured kernel for the point, hardware floor and shipped library for the ends. LOW 1.9 us is the minimum of that same measured distribution; the published silicon floor underneath it is lower still (an NVIDIA Quantum HDR switch is published at sub-130 ns port to port and a ConnectX-6 adapter at sub-600 ns, so roughly 1.3 us of the 2.03 is adapter and switch and the rest is protocol and software). HIGH 22 us is the shipped collective library: the same paper's Observation 5 puts *CCL an order of magnitude above MPI on small inter-node transfers, about 22 us at 1 B on Leonardo (Fig. 7b), and a decode-step all-reduce runs on NCCL rather than on the GPU-Aware MPI 1-byte ping-pong these point values are measured with. That asymmetry is the whole reason the band is now 11.6x wide rather than 1.5x wide, and the honest output of this correction is the BAND and not the point. MEAN-VERSUS-MEDIAN, recorded because it bounds how much the point can be trusted: the annotated Fig. 8a values are outlier-inflated means (LUMI same-switch box about 2.5 us against an annotated 3.71 us mean, Max 184.46 us; Leonardo across-group median about 2.6 us against a 4.23 us mean, Max 132 us -- the paper attributes this to network noise from other jobs). Only Alps same-switch (4.33, min 3.64 / max 5.2) and Leonardo same-switch (2.03, min 1.9 / max 2.4) are tight enough for the mean to stand in for the distribution, and this entry uses the second of those. DIRECTION: this correction makes the GPU side FASTER and moves the headline DOWN by roughly 0.73x, which is the direction that needs the least suspicion and is why it is applied at the point rather than only in the band.

hop_latency_s.note: WHAT THIS MODEL CHARGES A HOP FOR: one traversal of the NVSwitch tier. An A100 baseboard is a single all-to-all tier, so `collective_traversals` charges an in-domain all-reduce exactly two of them, and this model has no per-collective software term anywhere. This constant is therefore only ever consumed as 2 x hop = the WHOLE in-domain all-reduce at zero payload, and it has to be read as half a measured collective rather than as a wire delay. WITHDRAWN: the previous note's central claim, "NVIDIA publishes no NVLink or NVSwitch latency figure in any form -- six first-party pages were checked". NVIDIA does publish one, in the shipping source of its own collective library: NCCL's cost model carries hwLatencies[NVLINK][Ring][LL] = 0.6 us per NVLink ring step (src/tuning/cost_model.cc, byte-identical in v2.18.3-1 src/graph/tuning.cc), alongside 1.9 us for LL128 and 3.4 us for Simple, and NCCL's maintainer states the same three per-hop costs (about 1, 2 and 6 us) in NVIDIA's own issue tracker. A least-squares fit to a measured 2-to-8 GPU DGX A100 LL sweep gives 0.725 us per ring step on a 10.6 us fixed intercept, within 20% of NVIDIA's own constant. So the WIRE step is published and small; what a collective costs is set by a fixed software floor, and that floor is measured. WHAT IS MEASURED, at this model's granularity -- a whole 8-rank in-domain all-reduce at the smallest message, halved: best kernel 5.0 us, so 2.5 us per traversal (MSCCL++, ASPLOS 2026, 8x A100-40G over NVLink 3.0, 1 KB); MSCCL's all-pairs 9.5 us, so 4.75 us; stock NCCL 20.6 us, so 10.3 us. Four independent runs agree on the NCCL figure -- MSCCL++ Fig. 7 = 20.63 us; nccl-tests issue #149 on 8x A100-SXM4-80GB with NV12 between every pair = 20.65 us at 8 B and flat to 512 B; nccl-tests issue #123 on a DGX A100 with ALGO=Ring PROTO=LL = about 21 us; and NCCL's own cost model predicts 6.6 + 14 x 0.6 = 15.0 us. Point-to-point comparators, all third-party and all on fabricated A100 silicon: 3.65 us GPU-buffer to GPU-buffer through the six NVSwitches of a DGX A100 (Spetko et al., Energies 2021, Table 4 -- the same table measures 281.0 of the 300 GB/s this entry's `bytes_s` claims, so the bandwidth here is 6.8% optimistic too); 9.73 us one-way NCCL on two A100s (De Sensi et al. SC24 artifact, Zenodo 13312325); 10.4-13.5 us OSU MPI device-to-device on Polaris and Perlmutter (Siefert et al., SC-W 2023). STATED AT 2.5 us -- the best measured small-message all-reduce on this exact hardware, divided by the two traversals this model charges. It is the GPU-side twin of how `links.on_wafer` is now set: both sides are priced at the best measured kernel for their fabric, and both notes record that the library each vendor actually ships is 2-4x worse. The previous 1.5 us was BELOW every A100 measurement in existence -- it implies a 3.0 us in-domain all-reduce where the best measured is 5.0 us and the production stack measures 20.6 us -- so it flattered the GPU. Correcting it moves the headline UP, which is the direction that deserves the most suspicion, and is why the point is pinned to the best kernel rather than to NCCL. THE BAND. LOW 1.0 us is a 2.0 us in-domain all-reduce: below the 2.37 us best device-initiated kernel measured on GB200, which is a two-generation newer fabric, and above the 1.404 us speed-of-light floor those authors compute for it. That floor is 2 x 0.306 us L2 round trip + 0.792 us remote store; the previous note quoted the two terms as if they summed to 1.404 and they sum to 1.098, and only ONE of the three terms crosses the interconnect at all. LOW is deliberately GPU-favouring. HIGH 10.3 us is stock NCCL measured on this part, folded into the hop because the model has no term for a collective's fixed software cost. hop_latency_s.note: THIS IS THE N7-GENERATION ENTRY; ITS N5 TWIN IS `links.on_wafer_n5`. Until 2026-08-31 one wafer constant served BOTH studies while the GPU side already had two -- `nvlink3` at 2.5 us for the A100/N7 study, `nvlink5` at 1.2 us for the B200/4NP study -- so the N5/4NP study was charging the ROM side a 7nm-era wafer fabric against a 4nm-era NVLink. The split is now made; the N5 entry carries the WSE-3 derivation and the reason it lands on the SAME 125 ns, which is that the N7-to-N5 shrink went into the core rather than into the distance between cores and the clock did not move. Both sides of this comparison now scale with their node, or are stated equal for a reason. THE REST OF THIS NOTE IS THE N7 DERIVATION. WHAT THIS MODEL CHARGES A HOP FOR: one step between adjacent 815 mm2 reticle fields -- `reticle.area_mm2`, a 28.55 mm square -- of which one wafer holds 57. It is NOT a tile-to-tile hop and NOT a scribe-line crossing, and confusing them is a factor of 125: the single clock cycle Cerebras publishes is a hop between adjacent cores about 0.23 mm apart, and there are about 126 of those across one of this model's fields. Substituting the published one-cycle figure straight into this entry would give about 1.2 ns and would take the headline iso-area ratio from 8.33x to 14.7x. WHAT THE SOURCES MEASURE. (1) One cycle per core-to-core hop, ROUTER INCLUDED, is vendor-published for a shipping part -- WSE-3 white paper, "Each router uses lossless flow control with low buffering. This design enables single clock cycle latency between nodes"; Hot Chips 34, "Single cycle latency between cores" -- and independently stated on fabricated silicon by four peer-reviewed groups (Rocki SC20, Orenes-Vera ICS 2023, Luczynski HPDC 2024, Santos SC24). (2) Cerebras publishes the core grid outright at Hot Chips 34: die "17mm x 30mm", "66 x 154 Cores", core "228um x 170um", wafer "215mm x 215mm", "12 x 7 Die". (3) The clock is 850 MHz on every CS-2 in the literature and 1.1 GHz at Cerebras' stated design point. Cerebras publishes NO latency for the stitched reticle boundary itself in any document -- every vendor claim about it is about bandwidth or uniformity -- so the boundary is taken as one ordinary hop, which the end-to-end results below bound at no more than a few cycles. THE CONVERSION, stated so it can be checked: a field crossing costs (28.55 mm / core pitch) cycles / clock. WSE-2 at the published 0.224 mm geometric-mean pitch is 127 hops = 116 ns at 1.1 GHz to 150 ns at 850 MHz; WSE-3's geometry is not published at all -- see `links.on_wafer_n5`, where three published-input estimators put it at 126-131 hops against this 127, i.e. equal to within the method's resolution and if anything slower; CS-1 at the 89 x 51 tile grid Rocki publishes (0.348 mm) is 82 hops = 75-97 ns. Two MEASURED end-to-end results land inside that band. Rocki's full-wafer scalar AllReduce over about 380,000 processors takes "under 1.5 microseconds", which through this model's own 15.4 traversals at span 57 is at most 97 ns per field crossing. Santos et al. (SC24) state a wafer edge-to-edge latency "of around a microsecond", which the published geometry reproduces without adjustment (7 x 154 = 1,078 hops at 850 MHz = 1.27 us). The closest granularity match in existence is not Cerebras at all: Tesla publishes "100ns die-to-die latency" for a 645 mm2 reticle-class D1 die crossing to its neighbour inside a wafer-scale training tile (Hot Chips 34), and its own-die traversal scaled to 815 mm2 adds about 11 ns, so a bonded reticle-to-reticle step is about 111 ns. STATED AT 125 ns: the middle of the two N7 routes -- Dojo 111 ns bonded, Cerebras 116-150 ns stitched -- which is the node this entry prices. That is 25% ABOVE the 100 ns this entry previously assumed, so re-grading moved the constant AGAINST the side this study argues for. THE BAND, 75-250 ns, both ends evidenced rather than guessed. LOW is the coarsest tile pitch any wafer-scale part has shipped (CS-1's 0.348 mm, Rocki Fig. 2) at the fastest clock any vendor has published (1.1 GHz) -- and it is a real possibility rather than a formality, because a ROM region is a mask-ROM array and not a 38,000 um2 processing element, so a purpose-built design may legitimately put fewer routers across the same millimetres. Latency across a fixed distance is (distance / router pitch) x (1 cycle), so router pitch is the design choice this constant really encodes. HIGH is NOT a slower wire: it is the same wire under the collective the vendor SDK actually ships. Luczynski et al. measure Cerebras' own library running a corner-rooted X-Y AllReduce whose path is about 2x the mesh diameter, against the 1.1x diameter Rocki's hand-written kernel achieves and `MESH_ALLREDUCE_DIAMETER_FACTOR` charges; that 1.8x on the traversal count, folded into the hop because the model has no term for the collective algorithm, is about 230 ns, plus their measured 62-146 ns per-collective fixed floor which the model also has no term for. RETIRED: the previous 30-500 ns sweep. 30 ns requires 1.05 ns/mm, three times faster than the fastest axis any wafer-scale part has ever shipped; 500 ns is above every measurement in the literature. WITHDRAWN: the previous note's cross-check, "about 73 tiles across one 815 mm2 reticle field, so a reticle crossing is on the order of 73 cycles". It does not reproduce -- 900,000 cores over 46,225 mm2 is 15,868 cores in 815 mm2 and sqrt(15,868) = 126, not 73. The error was 1.7x and it ran in this study's favour.

hop_latency_s.note: THE N5 TWIN OF `links.on_wafer`, AND A NULL RESULT. This entry exists because one wafer-fabric constant was serving BOTH studies while the GPU side already had two -- `nvlink3` at 2.5 us for the A100/N7 study and `nvlink5` at 1.2 us for the B200/4NP study. `on_wafer` is derived from Cerebras WSE-2, a TSMC 7nm part, so the N6/N7 study was matched and the N5/4NP study was not: it charged the ROM side a 7nm-era wafer fabric against a 4nm-era NVLink, which understates the ROM side in exactly the study where it should be strongest. The wafer fabric is therefore node-keyed too, and this is the N5 entry, anchored on WSE-3 (TSMC 5nm, Hot Chips 2024). THE METHOD IS THE SAME ONE, DELIBERATELY -- two figures derived two ways are not comparable, which is the whole point of splitting the entry. A field crossing costs (28.55 mm / core pitch) cycles / clock, where 28.55 mm is sqrt(`reticle.area_mm2`), this model's reticle field edge, and the cycle is the vendor-published one-cycle core-to-core hop, router included. THE RESULT IS A NULL: N5 DOES NOT BUY A FASTER HOP, and this entry is therefore stated at the same 125 ns as its N7 twin. The method has exactly two terms and neither moved. (1) CORE PITCH DID NOT SHRINK. Cerebras publishes NO WSE-3 geometry. The Hot Chips 2024 successor to the WSE-2 slide that carried "17mm x 30mm", "66 x 154 Cores", "228um x 170um", "12 x 7 Die" and "215mm x 215mm" carries only three labels -- "10.7k Cores", "84 Die", "900k Cores" -- and every geometric dimension was dropped. What IS published bounds the pitch three ways, and all three land on or slightly ABOVE the N7 hop count of 127 per field: (a) the WSE-3 core is "approximately 38,000 um2 of silicon area in the TSMC 5 nm process" against WSE-2's published 228 x 170 = 38,760 um2, a 2.0% reduction, which at WSE-2's own fill fraction is 0.2218 mm of pitch and 129 hops; (b) 46,225 mm2 over the 900,000 ACTIVE cores is 0.2266 mm and 126 hops; (c) over the 970,000 PHYSICAL cores Cerebras states in its 2025 yield paper it is 0.2183 mm and 131 hops. The N7-to-N5 shrink went into the core, not into the distance between cores: the WSE-3 white paper gives the core the same 48 kB of SRAM, the same 110,000 standard cells and the same 50/50 logic-to-SRAM split as WSE-2, with the transistors spent on doubling the FP16 SIMD from 4-wide to 8-wide. Note the direction: a SMALLER core would make this constant WORSE. Latency across a fixed 28.55 mm is (distance / router pitch) x 1 cycle, so more routers per millimetre is more cycles per millimetre -- process scaling buys a mesh cores, not distance. (2) THE CLOCK DID NOT MOVE. Cerebras publishes 1.1 GHz for WSE-2 (Hot Chips 34, "Power efficient design point ... 1.1GHz clock frequency") and publishes NO WSE-3 clock in any document -- not the Hot Chips 36 deck, not the 2024 white paper, not the press release, not the product page. Two back-derivations from figures Cerebras DOES publish, each calibrated on WSE-2 where the answer is known, with every input stated so the arithmetic can be checked. MEMORY ROUTE, bandwidth / cores / the published 24 B per cycle SRAM port ("192-bit access per cycle from two 64-bit reads and one 64-bit write"): WSE-2 is 20 PB/s / 850,000 / 24 = 0.98 GHz against a published 1.1, so the method reads 1.12x low; WSE-3 is 21 PB/s / 900,000 / 24 = 0.97 GHz, or 1.00 GHz on the 21.6 PB/s the CS-4 datasheet's 43.2 PB/s implies for exactly half a WSE-3 Turbo -- corrected for the bias, 1.09 to 1.12 GHz. FABRIC ROUTE, bandwidth / cores / the published five-port router's 4 x 32-bit bidirectional interfaces (256 bit per cycle): WSE-2 is 220 Pbit/s / 850,000 / 256 = 1.01 GHz (bias 1.09x); WSE-3 is 214 Pbit/s / 900,000 / 256 = 0.93 GHz, corrected 1.01. So 1.01-1.12 GHz at N5 against 1.1 GHz published at N7: flat, inside a method whose own error on the calibration part is 9-12%. The 1.4 GHz that 2026 press reports quote for WSE-3 has NO vendor source -- it is a journalist's explicitly hedged inference ("I think", The Next Platform, 19 August 2026) back-read from the CS-4 launch -- and it is not used here. (3) THE BONDED ROUTE IS CHARGED AT BOTH NODES, WHICH IS THE CRUX. The N7 entry's 125 ns is the middle of TWO routes: Cerebras' stitched 116-150 ns and Tesla's bonded 111 ns, the latter from Dojo's published "100ns die-to-die latency" for a 645 mm2 reticle-class die inside a wafer-scale training tile, plus about 11 ns to scale its own-die traversal to 815 mm2 (Hot Chips 34, 2022). No bonded wafer-scale part has been published at N5. Withholding that route from the N5 entry -- which would put it at the stitched-only midpoint of about 132 ns and make N5 look WORSE than N7 -- would be applying a different method at the two nodes, and the whole reason for splitting this entry was that two figures derived two ways are not comparable. A bonded reticle interface is a packaging choice, not a property of the logic node, so it is offered to both. Both entries therefore blend the same two routes and differ only in the two node-dependent inputs above, neither of which moved. (4) WHAT THE NULL COSTS, STATED. 126-131 hops at N5 against 127 at N7 is -1% to +3% around the N7 figure, median estimator 1.6% SLOWER; the clock routes are flat to within their own bias. That is below the resolution of a method whose N7 input is itself rounded -- "17mm x 30mm" is a rounded 17.92 x 30.71, since 215/12 and 215/7 are what reproduce 46,225 exactly -- so the two nodes are stated EQUAL. Where the estimators do point they point SLOWER at N5, so stating them equal credits this study's own side by about 1.6% rather than costing it. Recorded here so it is not mistaken for a correction that went our way: a faster N5 wafer fabric would have RAISED the headline, and the evidence does not support one. THE STAKE, MEASURED: driving this entry alone to the low end of its own band, 75 ns, and re-simulating moves the N5 study's batch-1 headline from 5.85x to 8.03x and its DeepSeek-V4-Pro point at 554,700 mm2 from 4.01x to 5.00x, while leaving the N6 study unchanged to four decimals; driving `on_wafer` alone the same way moves N6 (10.78x to 13.95x) and leaves N5 unchanged. So the split is live and an N5-specific speed-up was worth up to 1.37x on that study's headline -- which is why it had to be derived rather than chosen. THE BAND, 75-250 ns, is the same as the N7 twin's and for the same two reasons, neither of which is a node argument. LOW is the coarsest tile pitch any wafer-scale part has shipped (CS-1's 0.348 mm, Rocki Fig. 2) at the fastest clock any vendor has published (1.1 GHz); it is a router-PITCH design choice, and a mask-ROM region is not a 38,000 um2 processing element, so a purpose-built design may legitimately put fewer routers across the same millimetres. HIGH is the same wire under the corner-rooted collective Cerebras' own SDK ships, which Luczynski et al. measure at about 2x the mesh diameter against the 1.1x `MESH_ALLREDUCE_DIAMETER_FACTOR` charges, plus their measured 62-146 ns per-collective fixed floor the model has no term for. NOT PUBLISHED AT EITHER NODE: the reticle-boundary crossing itself. For WSE-3 Cerebras states only that the fabric "crosses less than a millimeter of scribe line", that dies connect "at full performance" and that "software always sees a fully uniform 2D mesh" -- bandwidth and uniformity claims, never a latency. The boundary is taken as one ordinary hop at both nodes, which the end-to-end measurements cited on the N7 entry bound at no more than a few cycles.

clock_energy_j_per_mm2_per_cycle.note: 8.5e-11 J per mm2 per clock cycle for the clock network -- the distribution tree, its buffers and the clock pins it drives -- charged on every clocked mm2 whether or not a byte moves. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, 15% DOWN from the submitted 1.0e-10, which violated its own stated selection rule ('take the estimator that closes less of the gap' yields 8.48e-11 and the submission rounded up past it). WHAT THIS NUMBER ACTUALLY IS, and the note must say it plainly: clock distribution taken as 20-45% of a shipping NON-ANCHOR GPU's published TDP density, applied at that part's published clock. P100 is 300 W over 610 mm2 at 1480 MHz = 0.492 W/mm2 = 3.32e-10 J/mm2/cycle; GV100 is 300 W over 815 mm2 at 1530 MHz = 0.368 W/mm2 = 2.41e-10; 30% of each, geometric mean, is 8.5e-11. No node correction from 16FF+/12FFN to N7/N6 and no modern-clock-gating discount is applied, and the 20-45% band itself comes from 1992-2004 CPUs (Alpha 21064/21164, MCORE, XScale) with little fine-grain gating. THE SUBMITTED BOTTOM-UP ROUTE IS NOT A SECOND ESTIMATOR AND MUST NOT BE SOLD AS ONE: rebuilt on measured 7 nm primitives instead of its invented capacitance scaling (ASAP7 DFFHQNx1 measures 1.095 fJ/cycle against the Nangate45 DFF_X1's 3.626, a ratio of 0.302 where the submission assumed 0.116) and on this repository's own post-route SPEF-extracted clock tree (4.329 mW of clock group against 0.987 mW of raw CK pin load, a 4.39x distribution multiplier where the submission asserted 1.925x), it returns 578 W on an A100 rated at 400 W. It is reported as a CEILING CHECK THAT FAILS. What the A100's TDP actually bounds is the product of flip-flop areal density and enabled fraction, to about 63k/mm2 against the 435k x 0.59 = 257k the bottom-up assumed; that 4x is the honest statement of what is unknown here. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a published or measured clock-network power fraction for a post-2015 clock-gated GPU or accelerator (AccelWattch/GPUWattch-class validated breakdown, or a vendor statement). Range 3e-11 to 1.6e-10 spans ~12% (an aggressively gated part at a memory-bound decode step, XScale's 17% being the cited low outlier) to 45%, the top of the published band.
clock_energy_j_per_mm2_per_cycle.source: NVIDIA Ampere architecture whitepaper, die area / TDP / clock table for P100 (610 mm2, 300 W, 1480 MHz, 16FF+) and GV100 (815 mm2, 300 W, 1530 MHz, 12FFN), verified verbatim ; the 20-45% clock-network power fraction band from Dobberpuhl 1992, Restle 2001 and Donno 2004, which could not be re-fetched and is the single load-bearing input

rom_array.note: 0.15 -- a mask-ROM array's clocked leaf count per mm2 against a logic region's. VERIFIER'S CAUTION CARRIED, AND IT IS THE REASON THE RANGE REACHES 0.5: 0.15 was derived from a LEAF COUNT, but the measured post-route decomposition in this repository shows distribution -- largely wire, whose length is set by AREA and not by leaf count -- at ~3.4x the leaf pin load. Array-region clock power should therefore scale SUB-LINEARLY with leaf density, so 0.15 is likely optimistic for the ROM side and its low end needs a wire argument rather than a latch count. This multiplier and power.fabric_clock_hz multiply, and together they set the W/mm2 asymmetry between the two sides of the comparison this study exists to make, so they are swept jointly and never asserted.

clocked_idle_floor_w_per_device.note: 50 W per device of traffic-independent power, applied as a FLOOR on the enumerated static terms and not as an addend -- static power is max(leakage + clock + memory-interface idle, this) -- because leakage and clock ARE most of the physics inside a measured clocked-idle reading and adding both would double-count it. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, from 52 W and, more importantly, on SCOPE: the submission named this gpu_device_fixed_overhead_w and charged it to GPU-class devices only, which is the same class of error as a fitted multiplier and harder to see -- the evidence assembled for it says the floor is clock distribution plus memory-interface clocking on a large clocked die, and a compute-in-ROM part at 815 mm2 with a clocked ROM array and SRAM KV has both. It is charged to BOTH sides here. The value is the mean of four parts' clocked-idle fraction of TDP applied to 400 W: H100 SXM 72.5 W of 700 W = 10.357% (measured, NREL-class facility study); A100 SXM ~50 W of 400 W = 12.5%; B200 140 W of 1000 W = 14.0%; RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 77.03 W of 600 W = 12.84%, which is EXECUTED HERE and is the artifact named above. The submission's 84.6 W reading was REFUTED as an instrumentation artifact -- it averaged a window 4-10 s after a 411 W load stopped, which straddles the decay tail (t+0 s = 116.72 W, t+5 s = 76.95 W in the committed trace) -- and the replicated steady clocked-idle state is 77.03 W across 22 samples at 2610 MHz SM / 13365 MHz memory, util 0. Note what 'clocked' means: the same board at a genuinely idle P-state drops to 7.8 W median, so this is the floor for a device that is up and serving, not a power-gated one. Two caveats the submission hid: the two 'methods' were one, because the low-bandwidth sweep points were produced by duty-cycling and so return clocked-idle power by construction; and the P8 decomposition drops the memory clock 33x at the same time as the SM clock, so roughly 30 W of the 69 W delta is the memory subsystem, which is why memory_interface_idle_w_per_stack is a separate term. The published cross-check is independent and close: SC'25 Table 2 measures P_const = 54 W for the A100 (72 W GH200, 88 W MI250X GCD, 69 W MI300A). The 100 W upper end the submission proposed was REJECTED -- the A100's 100 W Min Power Limit is the lowest cap the driver will enforce, a policy floor and not a consumption measurement. The defensible top is the clocked-and-issuing figure, 80 W.
clocked_idle_floor_w_per_device.source: Executed on this machine: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, 600 W, 1,141 nvidia-smi samples, artifact committed at results/roofline/gpu_clocked_idle_floor.json. Published legs: Vercellino et al., Measurement of Generative AI Workload Power Profiles for Whole-Facility Data Center Infrastructure Planning, arXiv:2604.07345 (2026), Appendix A, 'each idle GPU spent 72.5 W on average' on 700 W H100 SXM ; Measuring the Energy of Data Movement on Modern GPU Systems, SC'25, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, Table 2 P_const = 54 W for the A100, as the independent cross-check

fabric_clock_hz.note: 1.0 GHz for a modelled design that has no published clock. WHAT THIS KEY FEEDS, STATED EXHAUSTIVELY, BECAUSE IT HAS BEEN MISREAD AS THE COMPUTE ROOF AND IT IS NOT: it is read in exactly one place, `Technology.clock_frequency_hz`, and consumed in exactly one, the clock leg of `device_static_power` -- clock watts per mm2 = `clock_energy_j_per_mm2_per_cycle` x this. IT SETS NO RATE. The compute roof on both sides comes from `compute.format_roofs_ops_s` divided by the anchor die area and scaled by `nodes.*.logic_density_vs_n7`, and it does not read this key; a published part uses its own `clock_frequency_hz` here and ignores this key entirely. So this constant reaches a rate ONLY through power -> thermal_scale, and only at points where thermal binds. WHERE IT IS NEVERTHELESS LOAD-BEARING FOR LATENCY, WHICH IS THE PART NOTHING ENFORCED: `latency.pipeline_fill_drain_s` and `latency.sequencer_issue_decode_s` are both DERIVED IN FABRIC CYCLES against this key and both bands are exact integer cycle counts at 1 GHz -- fill/drain 16 / 32 / 128 cycles, sequencer 1 / 3 / 8 cycles -- while neither entry reads it. Moving this key without moving those two silently breaks their stated derivations, and those two ARE on the critical path of every token on both sides. `tools/run_roofline_studies.py` now REFUSES that inconsistency: the consistency audit recomputes both entries' cycle counts at this frequency and fails if either point or either band end stops being the cycle count its own note claims. THE ASAP7 EVIDENCE WAS CHECKED AGAINST THIS CONSTANT AND DOES NOT RETIRE IT. This repository holds three routed, timing-PASSING ASAP7 blocks: `results/physical_abi3/asap7/reduction_s8_g2/pnr.json` at a 2.25 ns period (fmax about 455 MHz), `.../add_bf16_sram_engine/pnr.json` at 4.4 ns (about 239 MHz) and `.../matmul_bf16_sram_engine/pnr.json` at 18.0 ns (57.959 MHz). None closes at 1 GHz. FIVE REASONS THEY DO NOT RETIRE THIS KEY, IN DESCENDING ORDER OF FORCE. (1) They are not evidence about this quantity at all: this key sets clock ENERGY, and those are fmax figures for three specific blocks. (2) THE 18 ns PERIOD IS NOT A FABRIC CLOCK. `rtl/ot_ta_matmul_bf16_sram_engine.sv` is a serial reference executor: one 16-bit SRAM read per request/wait pair, and a combinational `fp32_mul_rne` feeding `fp32_add_rne` inside ONE cycle, unpipelined and unretimed. That cycle does ONE multiply-accumulate at most, and the state machine spends two cycles per MAC, so the hypothesis that the block does N MACs per cycle and that 58 MHz x N is consistent with 1 GHz is FALSE IN THE OTHER DIRECTION -- the block is slower than one MAC per cycle, not faster. What 18 ns measures is an unpipelined FP32 fused multiply-add plus a nonfinite check, which is a property of RTL written for arithmetic clarity rather than for frequency. (3) THE RULE. `docs/METHODOLOGY.md` SS 9 and the W9 claim boundary in `docs/UNIFIED_EXECUTION_CHECKLIST.md` both state that no frequency, area or energy from a 130 nm OR PREDICTIVE-7 nm open PDK may be scaled to N6/N5/N7/N4. That is not the SKY130 prohibition in W8.3 being silently extended: it is a separate rule that names predictive-7 nm explicitly, and this repository's own ASAP7 artifact declares its evidence class as "predictive open-PDK ... not a foundry PDK, not TSMC N7/N6/N5, not silicon". (4) THE 18 ns IS THE ARITHMETIC PACKAGE, AND THIS REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY MEASURED THAT SEPARATELY AND ATTRIBUTED IT TO A CODING SHAPE. OI-44 in `docs/UNIFIED_EXECUTION_CHECKLIST.md` synthesised each operation alone as one combinational cloud between registers: on SKY130 HD `ot_fp32_rne_pkg::fp32_add_rne` needs a 66.97 ns period (`results/physical_abi3/sky130hd/a3_numeric_probes/fp32_add.json`) and `fp32_mul_rne` needs 29.385 ns (`.../fp32_mul.json`), and the cause is recorded there as a 27-iteration cancellation-normalisation loop -- "a coding shape rather than a technology limit". The matmul engine's one cycle chains exactly those two functions, so the ASAP7 period is that package's delay and not a fabric's. Two further facts from the routed artifact itself put the same point beyond argument: `place_and_route.metrics.macro_count` is 0 and `sequential_cell_count` is 8,879, so the 256-entry input buffer and the 64-entry accumulator and auxiliary buffers are synthesised as flip-flop arrays, and every operand in that critical path is read through a combinational 256:1 and 64:1 register-file mux before it reaches the multiplier. No shipping fabric clocks a datapath shaped like that, and the block was never written to be one -- its header says it exists for bounded data-bearing execution and exact arithmetic. (5) ASAP7 IS PESSIMISTIC AND THE DIRECTION IS KNOWN: it is a predictive academic library with no foundry characterisation, no custom datapath cells, no SRAM compiler and conservative wire models, and the three blocks above were synthesised by an open flow from RTL with no pipelining, no retiming and no floorplanning. A predictive-PDK number is not silicon and none of the five reasons above is an argument that 1 GHz is RIGHT -- only that this evidence cannot set it. THE VALUE AND THE BAND ARE THEREFORE UNCHANGED at 1.0 GHz swept 0.5-2.0 GHz, AND THE BAND IS NOT WIDENED DOWNWARD ON THIS EVIDENCE. Note the direction that widening would run: no rate depends on this key, so lowering it buys clock power for free and RAISES the ROM side's thermal headroom, while the GPU comparators' clocks are published and do not move. A band widened to the ASAP7 fmax would be a one-sided credit to the ROM side bought with a number the methodology forbids using. THE SENSITIVITY IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED: `results/roofline/*/analytical.json -> fabric_clock_sensitivity` re-runs the study at both band ends and at the ASAP7 figures, with the two cycle-derived latency constants moved consistently, and reports what each does to every headline. WHAT THIS KEY IS WORTH ON THE HC1 POWER GATE, and the HC1 clock negative is registered HERE because Taalas publishes none: 0.5 GHz gives 70.16 W, 1.0 GHz gives 70.16 W (the 50 W clocked-idle floor binds below about 1 GHz, so the term is INERT there) and 2.0 GHz gives 75.81 W, moving the gate from 0.2807x to 0.3032x. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a published clock for any mask-ROM or compute-in-ROM inference die, or a foundry-PDK implementation of this program's own datapath at a target node.
fabric_clock_hz.source: no clock published for any mask-ROM or compute-in-ROM inference die; Taalas publishes no microarchitecture and no frequency (taalas.com, The Next Platform "Clock speed information is not disclosed", The Register, ServeTheHome, CNX, Wavect, Kaitchup, 13 Taalas patents with zero GHz/MHz hits, Hot Chips 2026 program, ISSCC 2026 advance program) ; checked against and NOT retired by this repository's routed ASAP7 blocks at results/physical_abi3/asap7/, which docs/METHODOLOGY.md SS 9 and the W9 claim boundary in docs/UNIFIED_EXECUTION_CHECKLIST.md ("no frequency, area or energy from a 130 nm or predictive-7 nm open PDK may be scaled to N6/N5/N7/N4") forbid scaling to a target node ; the 18 ns period is attributed to the arithmetic package by this repository's own SKY130 HD per-operation measurements at results/physical_abi3/sky130hd/a3_numeric_probes/

Sweep 0.4-0.8: at 0.4 the A100's leakage is 21.5 W and at 0.8 it is 41.4 W, so this parameter is worth about 20 W on a 400 W part. memory_interface_idle_w_per_stack.note: 2.8 W per HBM stack of traffic-independent DRAM device, PHY and controller power -- standby, refresh and an up-and-trained interface -- charged whether or not a byte moves. The submitted companion to the HBM energy term was filed as `measured` at 3.7 W/stack with a range of 3.27-4.27 and BOTH WERE REFUTED. The grade could not stand: its only source is an anonymous artifact-evaluation drop for a paper still under review -- no authors, no venue, no DOI -- and this file's own vocabulary reserves `measured` for fabricated silicon in a peer-reviewed venue. The range was false precision: both endpoints were the same 6.40 W measurement times two similar ratios, so they could not disagree. The honest interval is 1.2 W (DRAM device standby plus refresh, capacity-scaled from real HBM2 stack IDD2/IDD3N1 measurements of 272/246 mA at 1.2 V after subtracting a per-chip no-HBM baseline) to 6.40 W (a measured H200 memory-rail idle per stack, if HBM2e's subsystem idle is no lower than HBM3e's) -- a 5x band whose geometric centre is 2.8. This term is why clocked_idle_floor_w_per_device is a floor and not an addend: on the A100 the two describe overlapping physics, and SC'25's published P_const of 54 W is the whole traffic-independent draw that both are estimating. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: an Ampere-generation memory-rail measurement (Ampere does not expose the field), a vendor HBM2e stack IDD specification, or A100 baseboard rail telemetry.
memory_interface_idle_w_per_stack.source: HBM2 stack IDD2/IDD3N1/IDD5B measurements and an H200 memory-rail idle reading, both from the CMU-SAFARI/HBM-Power artifact drop (2026) for a paper under review -- no venue, no DOI, so this cannot be graded above `assumed` ; cross-checked against Measuring the Energy of Data Movement on Modern GPU Systems, SC'25, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, Table 2

power.purpose: Power a machine spends whether or not a byte moves. Before this block the model counted memory bytes and multiply-accumulates and nothing else, so it gave 54.21 W for an A100 against a published 400 W and 27.04 W for a Taalas HC1 against a published 200-250 W, and -- because step_time = raw_step_time x thermal_scale is the only path from power to any other quantity -- thermal_scale was exactly 1.0 at all 11,747 feasible points and no rate in the study depended on the energy model at all. Every term here is charged PER MM2 PER SECOND against the area split, not against traffic, which is what makes the thermal limit capable of binding. EVERY TERM IN THIS BLOCK WAS ADVERSARIALLY VERIFIED AND EVERY ONE WAS SENT BACK: the values below are the verifiers' corrections, not the submissions, and each note says which way the correction moved. Two of the corrections move power UP and two move it DOWN; none of them was chosen with a gate in view.

logic.note: 0.06 W per mm2 of STANDARD-CELL (logic) region at a 7 nm-class node, at 0.70-0.75 V and 85-105 C junction, on a mix weighted toward RVT. THE UNIT IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS THE SUBMISSION'S worst defect: it is per mm2 of standard-cell region, NOT per mm2 of die, so on a part that is mostly array this term is charged over the logic only. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, 2x UP from the submitted 0.03. The chain is: an executed ASAP7 place-and-route base of 0.74e-3 W/mm2 of 100%-filled cell area at 25 C/0.70 V typical (from this repository's own results/physical_abi3/asap7 metadata, cross-checked three ways against the liberty's 1 pW leakage unit and against real-scale ASAP7 cell areas), times a threshold-flavour mix, a temperature factor and a voltage factor. The correction is in the threshold ladder: the submission put RELATIVE per-flavour offsets (SLVT 0, LVT 0.071, RVT 0.142 V) inside an exponential that needs the ABSOLUTE saturation threshold, and a device with Vth = 0 is not off. That ladder predicts a 25->100 C ratio of 12.69x at typical/nominal, which is BELOW the 13.82x ASAP7's own SS liberty measures at a slower process AND a lower voltage -- impossible. Re-anchoring to absolute Vth_sat (RVT 0.24, LVT 0.169, SLVT 0.098 V, the lowest ladder clearing that floor) moves the combined mix x T x V factor from 14.8 to 25.3 at the low end and 62.4 to 114.8 at the point. The submission's structural claim that leakier flavours scale less steeply, so mix and temperature partly cancel, is separately FALSIFIED by the same library: measured INVx1 FF/TT ratios are 0.638 / 0.546 / 0.646 across RVT/LVT/SLVT -- flat and non-monotonic -- where the model needs a 1.5x spread. The high end 0.20 is CAPPED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY THE CHAIN: the chain's own 40/40/20 mix at 105 C and 0.85 V gives 0.43 W/mm2, which is 86% of thermal.cooling_limit_w_per_mm2 and is not physical for a shipping part; 0.19-0.20 is where an A100 lands at ~39% of TDP, the top of ReGate's measured 30-72% static-power band. Grade stays `assumed` and correctly so: ASAP7 is a predictive academic PDK, no datacentre die's Vt mix is published anywhere, and the absolute threshold ladder is inferred from Ioff-per-micron rather than read off a datasheet. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a foundry N7/N6 leakage-per-mm2 figure at a stated PVT, or an ASAP7 SRAM-flavour and LVT/SLVT SS liberty.

rom_array.note: 6.7e-3 W per mm2 of ROM ARRAY at a 7 nm-class node. WAS ZERO, DELIBERATELY, AND ZERO IS NOT PHYSICAL. The reason zero was defensible is now gone: the previous note held it at zero because the submitted companion of 0.006 W/mm2 had no derivation, and "a companion nobody derived is not evidence". A derivation now exists and it is built entirely on this file's own entries, so it can be checked line by line: the verified SRAM companion 0.005 W/mm2 over 24.07e6 usable bits/mm2 at 0.8 V is 0.260 nA per 6T cell; over 4 off devices in a 6T that is 0.065 nA per device; a NOR mask-ROM cell has ONE off device, so at this file's own ROM capacity density of 129.63e6 bits/mm2 (0.027 um2 6T cell x 0.33 ratio / 0.52 array efficiency) the array leaks 0.065 nA x 129.63e6 x 0.8 V = 6.73e-3 W/mm2. It rests on five `assumed` entries and is graded accordingly. THE DERIVATION DECLINES TWO REAL ROM-FAVOURABLE CREDITS, which is why it is safe at the point: an array with no read-stability constraint may use HVT or long-channel devices for free, and roughly half of a via-programmed NOR array's cells have no bitline leakage path at all. Qualitative corroboration that ROM array leakage is not negligible: TOM's entire third contribution is power-gating inactive ROM banks, 25.813 W down to 5.33 W. DIRECTION AND WHERE IT BINDS: this is a straight charge against the ROM side and it favours the GPU. On the current HC1 reconstruction the 432.4 mm2 ROM array contributes 2.90 W: it moves the static result from the 50.0 W clocked-idle floor to a 52.54 W enumeration and the whole gate from 85.0 W to 87.6 W -- and it matters on the wafer-class designs, where a 50 W per-device floor cannot bind and 6.7e-3 W/mm2 over hundreds of thousands of mm2 is thousands of watts. Sweep 1.3e-3 to 2.6e-2; note that `range_high` moves DOWN 13% from the incumbent 0.03, because the band is now a bracket around a derived point rather than the ceiling of an undocumented reconstruction, and that 13% is the only part of this edit that runs in the ROM side's favour.
rom_array.source: derived on this file's own entries: power.static_leakage_w_per_mm2.sram_array, sram.array_efficiency, nodes.N7.sram_hd_bitcell_um2, rom.cell_to_sram_cell_area_ratio and rom.array_efficiency, with one off device per NOR mask-ROM cell against four in a 6T ; qualitative corroboration from Guan et al., TOM, arXiv:2602.20662 (bank power gating 25.813 W -> 5.33 W)

sram_array.note: 0.005 W per mm2 of SRAM ARRAY at a 7 nm-class node. This companion's chain VERIFIED and is carried at the verifier's value, one third below the 0.015 that the same submission's 'of array' companion implied. 0.65 array efficiency over a 0.027 um2 N7 6T bitcell is 24.07 Mbit/mm2 of usable cells; at 0.05-1.0 nA of off current per cell and 0.8 V that is 0.96-19.3 mW/mm2, and the point sits at the geometric-centre end of it. Cross-check that reproduces: 537 Mbit at that density is 22.3 mm2 and 0.021-0.43 W. Charged over SRAM array area only -- the KV store on a ROM part, and the non-logic share of a published GPU die.

APPLY THIS ENTRY AND `rom.array_efficiency` IN ONE EDIT OR NOT AT ALL: what ROMA's figure actually fixes is the QUOTIENT ratio / array_efficiency = 0.6408, which with this file's published 0.027 um2 N7 6T cell gives ROM capacity density 57.8 Mbit/mm2 = 7.222 MB/mm2 against the 16.204 this file used to derive, a 2.243x correction AGAINST the ROM case. N5.note: N5 is the ROM node of the n5_vs_b200 study, compared against a B200 at 4NP. WHY THIS KEY IS NODE-ADDRESSED. This repository measured the via-programmed NOR ROM to 6T SRAM drawn-cell-area ratio at two nodes and got 0.1298 at 130 nm (IHP SG13G2, results/spice/ihp_sg13g2_bitcell/bitcell.json) against 0.2500 at a predictive 7 nm FinFET node (ASAP7, results/asap7_physical/bitcell_density/bitcell_density.json) -- 92.7% apart. WHAT THE SPLIT DOES NOT BUY, STATED PLAINLY SO NOBODY READS PRECISION INTO IT: N6 AND N5 CARRY THE SAME POINT AND THE SAME BAND, AND THE SPLIT MOVES NO NUMBER TODAY. The consistency audit in tools/run_roofline_studies.py therefore REFUSES any by-node value or band end that differs from the flat rom.cell_to_sram_cell_area_ratio until that one call takes the node it already has. THE BAND IS NOW EXECUTED, NOT MERELY DECLARED. The previous repair turned the prose-only "1/6 to 1/4" bracket into real range_low/range_high fields and made the audit refuse a band that excludes either committed measurement -- but nothing ever RE-RAN the study at those ends, so the stated uncertainty was still a claim rather than a result. results/roofline/*/analytical.json -> rom_cell_ratio_sensitivity now re-runs the whole study at both band ends and at all three ratios this repository has measured, reporting the chosen design, the ROM capacity density and the binding constraint on BOTH sides at each.

cim_cell_area_multiplier.note: area of a compute-in-ROM cell relative to a storage-only mask-ROM cell. A compute-in-ROM cell carries a pass transistor and the product-line wiring that lets it select one pre-computed partial product, on top of the via programming that stores its bits. Taalas describes one transistor per 4-bit parameter doing both, so the multiplier is small but cannot be 1.0. This is the second most load-bearing assumption in this file after the ROM-to-SRAM cell ratio, and it decides the storage-versus-compute-in-ROM comparison.
cim_cell_area_multiplier.source: no published compute-in-ROM bitcell at any node

cim_precompute_area_fraction.note: 0.18 of a compute-in-ROM die spent on the block that forms every product of one activation with the small weight alphabet, and on the accumulation that follows it. WAS 0.02, and THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE AGAINST 0.02 IS INTERNAL AND CHECKABLE: `src/opentallas/roofline.py` sets `compute_mm2 = cim_precompute_area_fraction * total_mm2` and that is the ONLY compute area a compute-in-ROM die is given -- there is no accumulator, adder-tree or partial-product-sum line item anywhere in that branch, and the ROM macro's 30% periphery budget is documented as decoders, sense amps and redundancy. At 0.02 the model charges a compute-in-ROM machine essentially nothing for summing the partial products it selects, which is a floorplan no fabricated compute-in-ROM part is near. The external leg is TOM (Guan et al., arXiv:2602.20662), stated in text: "The chip's total area is 56.9 mm2, with the majority (58%) allocated to our ... ROM. The on-chip SRAM ... and the distributed compute logic account for 24% and 18% of the area". Sweep 0.08-0.27. DIRECTION: favours the GPU, and it COMPOUNDS with the 2.243x ROM capacity-density correction -- it moves about 16% of the die from array to compute, cutting ROM from about 68% to about 52% of a compute-in-ROM die, so a compute-in-ROM point that fits today needs roughly 2.9x more ROM silicon under both corrections together.
cim_precompute_area_fraction.source: Guan et al., TOM, arXiv:2602.20662, area breakdown stated in text (58% ROM / 24% SRAM / 18% distributed compute logic on a 56.9 mm2 die) ; and this repository's own compute-in-ROM area branch in src/opentallas/roofline.py, which allocates no accumulator area at all

read_bandwidth_scaling_rule.note: Read-bandwidth density is scaled by (anchor-node bitcell area / target-node bitcell area): the same macro throughput in proportionally less area. No clock-frequency bonus is applied on top. For 28 nm -> N6 this ratio is 4.70x, which corresponds to an effective density-scaling exponent of 1.005 on (28/6) -- the wire/periphery-limited CONSERVATIVE end of the 1.0-2.0 bracket documented in src/opentallas/technology.py. src/opentallas/technology.py documents 1.0-2.0 as the plausible exponent bracket; this rule sits at its conservative end. HOW THIS DENSITY COUPLES TO CELL AREA, DECLARED BECAUSE THE MODEL CURRENTLY ANSWERS IT TWO DIFFERENT WAYS ONE FUNCTION APART AND NOTHING COMPARED THEM. `cell_area_coupling` = "none": `src/opentallas/roofline.py:rom_read_bytes_s_per_mm2` does not read `rom.cell_to_sram_cell_area_ratio` at all, so moving that ratio scales CAPACITY density and leaves READ-BANDWIDTH density untouched -- measured at N6, 0.33 -> 0.11 takes capacity 7.295 -> 21.886 MB/mm2 while bandwidth stays 282.222 GB/s/mm2, and the full-array sweep therefore moves 25.85 -> 77.55 us, a 3.0x swing on the ROM lane's hard floor. `cim_cell_area_coupling` = "proportional": one function away, `rom_read_bytes_s_per_mm2_for` divides bandwidth density by `rom.cim_cell_area_multiplier` exactly as `rom_bits_per_mm2_for` divides capacity, and its own docstring gives the reason -- a larger cell means fewer cells per mm2 and "no extra bitlines and no sense amps", so the rate per mm2 falls in the same proportion the capacity does and THE SWEEP IS INVARIANT (25.85 us at both policies, measured). THESE TWO CANNOT BOTH BE RIGHT. Both constants are cell AREA and both sit in the same density chain: if a bigger compute-in-ROM cell costs bandwidth per mm2 because it adds no bitlines, then a bigger storage cell costs it for the same reason, and the sweep should be invariant to `cell_to_sram_cell_area_ratio` too. The opposite reading is defensible -- read bandwidth may be set by sense amps and IO that do not shrink with the bit cell, in which case bandwidth density really is roughly cell-size-independent and only capacity scales -- but the model does not get to hold both readings at once without saying which is which, and until this field existed it held both and said neither. NOTHING IS TUNED HERE AND NEITHER READING IS ADOPTED: the observed coupling of each constant is now MEASURED by the consistency audit in `tools/run_roofline_studies.py`, which refuses the file if either stops matching the string declared here. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a published mask-ROM macro family at one node with two bit-cell pitches and its read bandwidth stated for both, or a routed ROM macro in this repository at two drawn pitches -- `results/spice/ihp_sg13g2_rom_macro/macro_route.json` is one pitch. THE FIX IS NOT IN A FILE THIS CHANGE OWNS: it is `src/opentallas/roofline.py:rom_read_bytes_s_per_mm2`, and it is reported rather than made, because choosing a reading without evidence would move the ROM side's hard floor by 3.0x on nothing.
